investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the underlying VM-backed pod never left the Pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and the remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Because no schedulable node exists and preemption found no victims, every remote-agent pod remains stuck in Pending, preventing VM provisioning and causing all downstream evidence (vmIdPresent, remoteState, agentId, orgId) to go uncollected. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity or configuration constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable root cause, pod stuck for 147s, 0/6 nodes available, same kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion message.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent===true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod is unscheduled.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=130697 (~130s), consistent with the scheduler timeout window reported in the failure message (pod stuck for 124s).
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes; the other 4 nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of general resource availability.

[Possible] The cluster has not scaled out additional kata-capable nodes to meet demand, either because autoscaling is not configured for this node pool, the autoscaler has not yet reacted, or the node pool has reached its maximum size.
[Possible] A prior eval run or other workload left remote-agent VMs running and not cleaned up, consuming the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots that would otherwise be available to new pods.

[Lower confidence] A configuration change in the node affinity/selector or resource request for remote-agent pods could have narrowed the schedulable node set, but no suspect change targeting pod scheduling configuration appears in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion on Production Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-15T20:40–20:45Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule new kata peer-pod VMs because 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned an agent, and consequently none of the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were produced, causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail with zero evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm (production-api environment, 6 nodes) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, while the other 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector for peer-pod scheduling. This makes every new remote agent pod Unschedulable. The eval runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1905) calls createAgent with type "remote", which triggers peer-pod VM provisioning; that provisioning stalls, the pod remains pending for 143 s (remote-agent-state), 124 s (remote-agent-create), and 147 s (remote-agent-runtime), and the probe times out before any agent identity or state is returned. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents peer-pod node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the underlying VM-backed pod never left the Pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and the remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Because no schedulable node exists and preemption found no victims, every remote-agent pod remains stuck in Pending, preventing VM provisioning and causing all downstream evidence (vmIdPresent, remoteState, agentId, orgId) to go uncollected. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity or configuration constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 124s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable root cause, pod stuck for 143s, 0/6 nodes available, same kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion message.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable root cause, pod stuck for 147s, 0/6 nodes available, same kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion message.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, confirming the pod never reached a running state where the runner could collect them.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}), consistent with the probe aborting before any VM identity or state could be recorded.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) which must provision a VM-backed pod; if that pod never schedules, no evidence is written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent===true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod is unscheduled.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=130697 (~130s), consistent with the scheduler timeout window reported in the failure message (pod stuck for 124s).
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes; the other 4 nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of general resource availability.

[Possible] The cluster has not scaled out additional kata-capable nodes to meet demand, either because autoscaling is not configured for this node pool, the autoscaler has not yet reacted, or the node pool has reached its maximum size.
[Possible] A prior eval run or other workload left remote-agent VMs running and not cleaned up, consuming the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots that would otherwise be available to new pods.

[Lower confidence] A configuration change in the node affinity/selector or resource request for remote-agent pods could have narrowed the schedulable node set, but no suspect change targeting pod scheduling configuration appears in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, meaning the effective scheduling pool is already small and any VM slot contention immediately causes unschedulability.
